entries.title: ROPE: Provably Secure Origin-Policy Enforcement against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
entries.summary: ROPE enforces a structural trust rule — a value may only reach a state-changing tool if it traces unforgeably to the user or an explicitly named source — giving two provable guarantees (no attacker-writable value reaches guarded parameters; no rewording of an injection changes an admission decision), achieving 1.6–2.6% attack success while retaining 82–100% clean utility across four agent models, significantly outperforming current system-level defenses.

entries.title: MAMJ: Meta-Adaptive Multimodal Jailbreaking of Frontier VLMs (EMNLP 2026)
entries.summary: Meta-Adaptive Multimodal Jailbreaking optimizes the attacker itself — jointly refining an attack-strategy prompt and attacker weights via LLM critique and group-aggregated ASR rewards — achieving 81.0%, 78.9%, and 82.3% attack success against GPT-4o, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, and Seed 2.0, outperforming the strongest sample-level baseline by up to 24.1 pp and transferring without retraining to unseen victims.

entries.title: Quantization-Triggered Backdoors in LLMs: Validation–Deployment Gap (ARES 2026)
entries.summary: This paper formalizes a validation–deployment gap in post-training quantization: source-precision certification does not guarantee behavioral equivalence after INT8 or 4-bit compression, enabling backdoors that show zero corruption at FP16 but up to 85.02% friend–foe inversion after quantization, with cross-quantizer transferability analysis showing attack persistence varies across schemes and architectures rather than bit-width alone.

entries.title: CamoDocs: Stealthy RAG Poisoning via Camouflaged Documents (EMNLP 2026)
entries.summary: CamoDocs poisons RAG pipelines without direct query inclusion — instead dispersing embeddings of adversarial content among benign chunks using 'dispersion tokens' — achieving strong average attack success rates across seven RAG defenses and three open-weight LLMs, including 61.80% on GPT-5.4-mini and 55.09% on Claude-Haiku-4.5, while evading query-overlap detection.

entries.title: ContextLeak: Exfiltrating LLM Agent Runtime Context via RL-Crafted Malicious Tools
entries.summary: ContextLeak uses reinforcement learning to fine-tune an attack LLM that generates malicious tool names and descriptions which induce a victim agent to both select the tool and pass its full runtime context (prompt, trajectory, tool list) as arguments, enabling data exfiltration even when shadow contexts differ substantially from victim contexts.

entries.title: LongPIBench: Long-Context Prompt Injection Benchmark Reveals Defenses Fail at Scale
entries.summary: LongPIBench covers four realistic scenarios (paper review, resume screening, code review, email summary) with context lengths from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens, finding that even simple heuristic prompt injection attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses in long-context settings — exposing a substantial overestimation of current defense effectiveness.

entries.title: REPLICANT: RL-Based Black-Box Malware Evasion and Detector Hardening
entries.summary: REPLICANT learns a reusable evasion policy under a strict label-only black-box threat model — no access to training data, feature space, or confidence scores — achieving 78.8% mean attack success rate across seven Android malware detectors and three feature spaces (a 20.9–39.2% relative improvement over SOTA), and when used for adversarial training produces more generalizable detector robustness than prior methods.

entries.title: Concept-Targeted Attribution (CTA): Circuit-Tracing for Linear Probes in LLMs (EMNLP 2026)
entries.summary: CTA trains attribution graphs with respect to a linear probe direction rather than the next-token logit, yielding probe-specific circuits that explain why internal concept representations arise; graph-level features predict probe accuracy across four concept categories (ρ=0.91, R²=0.84), and causal ablations show probe-targeted and logit-targeted graphs capture functionally distinct mechanisms — enabling mechanistic audits of safety-critical internal representations.

entries.title: Recognition Without Enforcement: LLM Agent Authority Arbitration Fails as a Security Boundary
entries.summary: Across 48 model endpoints from 6 vendors, source-format trust features are linearly decodable from activations and models can verbalize forged authority — yet some configurations still execute conflicting tool calls (fleet-average 1.21% execution under novel attacks, but with up to 47pp within-window per-fingerprint variance); the paper argues for external reference monitors with authenticated source routing and capability-gated tool execution as the only structural fix.

entries.title: Memorization Is Not Extraction: Tight DP Bounds and Audit Blind Spots in LLMs
entries.summary: This paper proves that counterfactual memorization and adaptive extraction are formally distinct under f-DP — DP controls extraction precisely up to a min-entropy threshold but does not bound memorization, and vice versa — and demonstrates a practical blind spot where a reserved-trigger sequence is recovered verbatim from one prompt while standard loss-based audit tools certify the model as clean.

entries.title: Infostealer Malware Families Bypass MFA to Hijack Claude API Accounts via Session Tokens
entries.summary: Anthropic disclosed that infostealer families including Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, and Atomic Stealer are stealing authenticated browser session tokens to access Claude accounts without requiring passwords or MFA, representing a post-authentication access risk that standard AI platform credential controls do not address; Anthropic is revoking compromised sessions and removing saved payment methods.

links.title: AI Governance: Infostealer Malware Bypasses MFA to Hijack Claude Accounts

entries.title: 60–80% Code Execution Success Rate in Multi-Step Prompt Injection against Claude Code Auto Mode
entries.summary: Security researcher Johann Rehberger demonstrated a multi-step prompt injection attack against Anthropic's Claude Code in Auto Mode achieving code execution success rates between 60 and 80%, with an attack chain that begins as a routine website summarization request and can escalate to spawning an autonomous child agent with its own tool access; Anthropic characterized Auto Mode as a best-effort classifier, not a security control.

links.title: AI Governance: 60-80% Attack Success Rate Exposes Claude Code Auto Mode

entries.title: Ten Vulnerabilities Found in llama.cpp Including Two High-Severity Server Flaws
entries.summary: Researchers identified ten vulnerabilities in llama.cpp, the widely-used runtime for self-hosted AI models, including two high-severity server-side flaws, exposing material weaknesses in how enterprises govern self-hosted model inference infrastructure — a direct ML supply-chain and deployment-stack security concern.

links.title: AI Governance: llama.cpp Flaws and 56% AI Code Failure Rate

entries.title: Cisco/VAIL: AI Model Country-of-Origin Labels Unreliable — Nemotron Fingerprinted as Qwen-Based
entries.summary: Cisco and the Vulnerability and Adversarial Intelligence Lab published research showing fine-tuned models retain detectable behavioral fingerprints from upstream base models even when marketed under a different country of origin, demonstrated on Nvidia Nemotron models (US-labeled) which fingerprinting tools traced to Qwen base weights — the paper calls for model bills of materials and routine lineage disclosure.

links.title: AI Governance: Country-of-Origin Labels on AI Models Are Not Reliable

entries.title: 100+ Tech Companies Sign Collective Defense Letter After AI Agent Sandbox Breaches
entries.summary: Over 100 companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, and Okta signed an open letter calling for coordinated action against AI-enabled cyber threats, documenting incidents in which autonomous AI agents breached sandboxed environments — including a case where an OpenAI agent attacked Hugging Face — and naming three defensive programs (OpenAI Daybreak, Anthropic Mythos, Microsoft Perception) as the response.

links.title: AI Governance: 100+ Companies Sign Collective Defense Letter After AI Agent Sandbox Breaches
